draft.emotion: hopeful and fresh, looking toward the future with energy
notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine ('un hombre joven', 'una mujer joven'). The plural adds a written accent to keep the stress on the first syllable: 'jóvenes'.
Also used as a noun meaning 'young person' ('el joven', 'la joven'); in Mexico, it is commonly used to politely address a young waiter or clerk.

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for only a short time; not old.

examples.text: Mi hermana es muy joven todavía.
examples.translation: My sister is still very young.

examples.text: Los jóvenes buscan su primer trabajo.
examples.translation: The young people are looking for their first job.

draftBefore.emotion: hopeful and fresh, looking toward the future with energy
notes: Used for both people and things. When referring to people, it can also function as a noun, meaning 'young person' (el joven/la joven).
It is different from 'nuevo', which means 'new' (recently made or bought). Use 'joven' for living beings or concepts like 'a young company'.

senses.definition: Having lived only a short time; not old.

examples.text: Mis abuelos son muy activos a pesar de no ser jóvenes.
examples.translation: My grandparents are very active despite not being young.
examples.emotion: affectionate and respectful, celebrating their energy

senses.definition: In an early stage of development.

examples.text: Esa empresa es muy joven pero tiene mucho éxito.
examples.translation: That company is very young but it is very successful.
examples.emotion: impressed and optimistic about the future
